question.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix 
$P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 4 \\ 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(P-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 4 \\ 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(3-\lambda )-2\cdot 4 & =0 \\ 3-\lambda -3\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-8 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda -5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot (-5)}}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{36}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 6}{2} \\  & =5,-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =-1$ and $\lambda =5.$
